accessibility.accessibleNameSource: label prop. Without a label the viewport stays focusable but is not exposed as a region, and a console warning fires once per element.
aria: viewport: tabindex=0, role=region and aria-label only while content overflows, so every scrollable area can be reached and operated without a mouse (WCAG 2.1.1)
a resize observer re-evaluates overflow when the viewport or the content changes size; it is re-attached when the element is moved in the DOM
scrollbars are native, styled with scrollbar-width and scrollbar-color

keyboard.Tab: focus the viewport while it can scroll

antiPatterns.alternative: Set height or max-height on the host
antiPatterns.pattern: A scroll area with no height or max-height
antiPatterns.why: It grows with its content and never scrolls
Wheel and keyboard scrolling get trapped

useCases.use: sb-scroll-area with a height and a label
useCases.when: A bounded panel (list, log, code) that must scroll inside a fixed size
Content that is also wider than its container

anatomy.name: viewport
anatomy.notes: The native scroll container (overflow auto on the enabled axes). Focusable and a region only while content overflows.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.notes: Wraps the slotted content so growth can be observed.

default.notes: Any content, plus optional sb-scroll-bar children that choose the scrolling axes.

orientation.note: The axis to enable. A scroll area with no sb-scroll-bar scrolls vertically; with some, it scrolls on exactly the axes they name.

elements.summary: Declares which axis the scroll area scrolls on. The scrollbar itself is native; this element only switches the axis on.

openQuestions.answer: Native, so wheel, touch, drag and keyboard stay the browser's; style with scrollbar-width and scrollbar-color. sb-scroll-bar only declares the axis.
openQuestions.question: Custom scrollbar elements or native scrollbars?

openQuestions.answer: The viewport gets tabindex=0 and role=region with an aria-label while it overflows.
openQuestions.question: How do keyboard users reach the content?

openQuestions.answer: color.input (3:1 on the background); the reference's border color is too light for WCAG 1.4.11.
openQuestions.question: Scrollbar thumb color?

label.note: Accessible name of the scrollable region. Required for a good experience: it names the focus stop that keyboard users land on.

scrollable.note: The viewport becomes a focus stop and a named region.
scrollable.trigger: content is larger than the viewport on an enabled axis

contract.summary: A region that scrolls its content natively, with themed thin scrollbars and keyboard access when there is something to scroll to.

# Plan: Scroll Area (planning gate)

Status: Approved under SB-0011 (owner pre-approval, 2026-11-08).

## Scope
`sb-scroll-area` (label) and `sb-scroll-bar` (orientation, axis marker). Native overflow, themed thin scrollbars, keyboard access while scrollable. Out of scope: custom-drawn scrollbars, scroll-linked events, hover-only scrollbars.

## Files (in build order)
| Step | File |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | `src/components/scroll-area/ScrollArea.stories.ts` |
| 2 | `playwright/tests/scroll-area/scroll-area.behavior.spec.ts` (written first, must fail) |
| 3 | `src/components/scroll-area/ScrollArea.scss` -> `ScrollArea.styles.ts` (generated) |
| 4 | `ScrollArea.ts`, `ScrollBar.ts`, `index.ts` |

## Test plan (test-first)
- Native vertical scrolling; horizontal only with a horizontal sb-scroll-bar.
- Scrollable: tabindex 0, region named by label; not scrollable: neither.
- Keyboard scrolling with arrows after Tab; keyboard-only focus ring.
- Scrollbar styling from tokens; overflow re-checked when content grows; one-time missing-label warning; axe.

## Accessibility deviations from the references
- The reference draws its own scrollbar parts and has no keyboard stop; this uses native scrollbars and adds the focus stop. Thumb uses `input` for 3:1.

## Open questions (recommendation first)
All three answered with the recommendation: native scrollbars with an axis marker element; focus stop and region while overflowing; `input` thumb color.
